wheel.lug_torque: 83 lb-ft (110 N·m) per Toyota's 1999–2002 owner's manuals

max_tire.note: Toyota-4Runner.org consensus (about 31.6 in); wide aggressive treads or spacers can rub at full compression
One owner reports no rub on 16x8 wheels with 4.5 in backspacing and about 2 in of front lift (not yet wheeled)
Common 33-in setup; expect to fold the pinch weld and trim the fender liner, and keep backspacing around 4–4.5 in. Spacers make it worse

items.title: Missing utility-vehicle warning label
items.summary: The required rollover warning sticker was not fitted to the driver's sun visor.

items.title: Stability under heavy load and severe steering
items.summary: Loading to both rear axle rating and GVWR plus a severe manoeuvre could cause the 2WD 4Runner to lose directional stability.

items.title: Front lower ball joints
items.summary: Scratched ball surface can cause excessive wear and looseness in the lower ball joint.

timeline.change: All-new Prado-based chassis: coils all round, rack-and-pinion, dual airbags, 3RZ-FE four or 5VZ-FE V6, optional rear e-locker
New switch panels and four-spoke steering wheel with redesigned airbag
Facelift ('fat lip' bumper, multi-parabola headlights), new dash; optional Multi-Mode transfer case. IH8MUD regulars rate 1999–2000 the best years, a '99 with the E-locker above all
Manual gearbox dropped (last manual 4Runner); rear e-locker still optional. The other half of the forum-favourite 1999–2000 pair
Four-cylinder dropped; VSC and Multi-Mode standard on 4WD; rear e-locker replaced by traction control

identify.intro: Plenty of 3rd gens for sale are two-wheel-drive, four-cylinder or locker-less, and the locker is the option that sets prices.

items.head: Model codes
items.body: US trucks are RZN180/185 (2.7 3RZ-FE four) or VZN180/185 (3.4 5VZ-FE V6). KZN185 and KDN185 are Japanese diesel Hilux Surfs.

items.head: Rear e-locker
items.body: Optional on 4WD trucks from 1996 to 2000, never standard on any trim per a 1997 brochure cited by owners, and gone for 2001–02. Look for the dash switch, the actuator and wiring on the rear diff, and the factory locker placard. A locked rear diff also takes more oil: 2.75 L vs 2.45 L.

items.head: Facelift tells
items.body: 1999–2000 trucks have the 'fat lip' bumper and multi-parabola headlamps; 2001–02 add clear tail lamps, a new grille and five-spoke wheels; 2002 adds chrome liftgate trim.

items.head: Transfer case
items.body: 1996–98 4WD trucks use a part-time lever (Limiteds use a pushbutton for H4); Multi-Mode was optional from 1999 and standard on 4WD from 2001.

values.intro: Prices are strong and rising; low-mile, unmodified SR5s and Limiteds, especially lockered 1996–2000 trucks, sit at the top.
values.note: Based on 24 Bring a Trailer sales from August to October 2026 (median about $18,750). The top sale was a 41k-mile 1997 SR5 4WD at $38,250.

paragraphs: Japan's Hilux Surf (N185) came with diesels never sold in the US: the 3.0 1KZ-TE turbo-diesel (1995–2000) and the common-rail 1KD-FTV (2000–02). Once a Surf is 25 years old it can be imported without meeting US federal safety standards. Per BE FORWARD, the first 2001 models crossed that line in 2026, so late 1KD-FTV trucks are only now becoming eligible. They are right-hand drive, and state titling and emissions rules still apply.

production.intro: Built at Tahara and at Hino's Hamura plant from August 1995 to August 2002; its 1997 US sales of 128,496 stood as the 4Runner record until the 5th gen passed it in 2018.
